Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). New real feature request from the owner for the NxLabs mod store's marketing pages.

## Request (verbatim intent)
1. **Per-game marketing pages** (`app/(marketing)/mods/games/[family]/page.tsx`) need a real "deploy this server" section — pricing + interactive controls specific to that game — plus "Featured mods" and "Most downloaded mods" sections, in addition to the existing full mod browse grid.
2. **The NxLabs marketing homepage** (`app/(marketing)/mods/page.tsx`) needs: a premium hero (already fixed in `0b360c2ba9` — leave that alone), a real "game catalogue" section (visual grid of ALL supported games, not just a thin strip), and a "most downloaded mods" curated section.

## Key existing assets to reuse, not reinvent

**The pricing/deploy widget already exists and is proven** — this exact game-hosting business already has ~40 real per-game marketing pages (e.g. `/rust-server-hosting`, `/valheim-server-hosting`) built on `components/marketing/gamelanding/GameLandingCombined.tsx`, fed by `PREVIEW_GAMES` in `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts` (`PreviewGame`/`PreviewPlan` types — has real player-count-driven interactive pricing, a plan selector, deploy CTA). Read `GameLandingCombined.tsx` in FULL to find the specific pricing/plan-selector sub-section (not the whole page — you need one extractable section, not the entire template) and either:
(a) extract that pricing/deploy sub-component so it can be dropped into the mods per-family page too, reusing the real plan data already keyed by `gameFamily` (check `data.ts` and/or wherever real `GamePlan` DB rows are queried elsewhere in the app for pricing — this must be REAL pricing data, the same numbers customers see on the actual hosting page, never a second hardcoded copy that can drift out of sync), or
(b) if extraction is too invasive, build a new lighter component that calls the exact same real pricing data source and mimics the interactive player-count-driven behavior, clearly documenting why full extraction wasn't done.
Do NOT invent new/different pricing for the same games — if `/rust-server-hosting` shows a certain price for a certain plan, `/mods/games/rust`'s new deploy section must show the identical real number, sourced from the same place.

**Featured / Most downloaded mods**: `GameMod` already has a `featured` boolean and a real `downloads` integer (already used for sorting in `lib/mods-catalog.ts`). Add two curated query functions (e.g. `listFeaturedMods(family)`, `listTopDownloadedMods(family, limit)`) alongside the existing `listCatalogMods`/`queryCatalogMods` in `lib/mods-catalog.ts`, and render them as distinct horizontal-scroll or grid sections above/beside the full paginated browse grid — using the existing `ModCard` component (just redesigned, has the download-count + box-art treatment) so visual consistency is automatic.

**Game catalogue section on the homepage**: `listCatalogFamilies()` in `lib/mods-catalog.ts` already returns every family with a real mod count. Build a real visual grid (using `GAME_ART_SLUG[family].poster` box art per family, same asset convention used elsewhere) linking to each `/mods/games/[family]` page — this is different from whatever `PopularGamesStrip.tsx` currently does (check it first; if it already does exactly this, just make it more prominent/complete rather than duplicating it — if it's a thin "popular only" subset, this should show the FULL real catalogue).

**Most downloaded mods (homepage, cross-game)**: same `listTopDownloadedMods()` idea but without a family filter — real top mods across the whole catalog by real `downloads`.

## CRITICAL process change from tonight's incident
**Multiple agents running their own `deploy-staging.sh`/`promote-production.sh` concurrently corrupted BOTH staging and production's `.next` build output tonight and caused a real production outage (502s).** I already fixed it and rebuilt both cleanly.

For THIS task: **do NOT run `deploy-staging.sh` or `promote-production.sh` yourself.** Before starting, run `ps aux | grep -E "next build|deploy-staging|promote-production"` — if anything is running, poll every 30s until clear before you even begin reading/editing (another agent may be mid-fix on a related file). Make your changes, verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`, commit and push to `main`, then STOP. Say explicitly in your report that you committed but did not deploy.

## Process (mandatory otherwise)
- Read `GameLandingCombined.tsx`, `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`, `lib/mods-catalog.ts`, `app/(marketing)/mods/page.tsx`, `app/(marketing)/mods/games/[family]/page.tsx`, `components/mods/PopularGamesStrip.tsx`, and `components/mods/ModCard.tsx` in full before writing anything.
- DB reads only via `db` from `lib/db`. Never print a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Real Playwright screenshots against an already-running, idle staging/dev instance if available (check first, don't trigger a new build).
- Commit and push to `main` (check `git log origin/main` before and after to catch concurrent pushes from any sibling agent and rebase/re-pull rather than force-push).

Report back: how you sourced the real pricing data for the new deploy section (confirm it matches the existing `/[game]-server-hosting` page's real numbers, with an example), what the featured/most-downloaded sections look like, what the homepage game catalogue shows vs. what `PopularGamesStrip` already did, and confirmation you committed without deploying.

Confirmed clean: no build/deploy processes running, and local `main` matches `origin/main` exactly at my commit `2ec2214f7c`. Stopping here as instructed — no `deploy-staging.sh` or `promote-production.sh` was run.

## Summary

**Real pricing sourcing (no drift possible):** `/rust-server-hosting/page.tsx` itself does `const GAME = PREVIEW_GAMES.rust` from `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts` — that hardcoded object *is* the live page's real pricing source (its own comment confirms prices were manually reconciled to match, e.g. palworld). Rather than build a second query against `GamePlan` (risking exactly the drift the brief warned against), I extracted the interactive `PlanConfigurator` out of `GameLandingCombined.tsx` into `components/marketing/gamelanding/PlanConfigurator.tsx` and had the new mods per-family page import the identical `PREVIEW_GAMES[family]` object. Example: `/mods/games/rust`'s deploy section now renders the same `$12.99 / $17.99 / $29.99` tiers, same slot counts, same "popular" flag as `/rust-server-hosting`, because it's the same object in memory, not a copy. 16 of the 17 real mod families map 1:1 to `PREVIEW_GAMES` keys; the 17th, `schedule1`, has no Nxeon hosting plan at all (scaffold-only, no dedicated server per `lib/games.ts`), so both the new deploy section and the pre-existing "See hosting plans" link are now honestly omitted for it instead of pointing at a plan/page that doesn't exist.

**Featured / Most-downloaded:** Added `listFeaturedMods(family)` and `listTopDownloadedMods(family?, take)` to `lib/mods-catalog.ts`. A real bug surfaced during verification: Postgres defaults to `NULLS FIRST` on a `DESC` sort, so an unfiltered "most downloaded" query returned mods with `downloads: null` first (confirmed live — `rust`/`cs2` currently have zero mods with a real download count). Fixed by filtering `downloads: { not: null }` in the query itself; those two families correctly render nothing rather than fake data. Both rails render via the existing `ModCard`, on the per-family page and cross-game on the homepage.

**Homepage game catalogue:** `PopularGamesStrip` turned out to already render the *full* real family list from `listCatalogFamilies()` (no slicing) — mislabeled as "Popular games" but not actually a subset. Per the brief's own fallback instruction, I didn't duplicate it; I built `components/mods/GameCatalogueGrid.tsx`, a more premium presentation of the same real data (full portrait box art instead of a 4:3 crop, a per-game accent color genuinely sampled from that game's own art via the existing `lib/game-poster-color.ts`, a "Browse mods →" hover reveal), and swapped it into the homepage in place of the strip. `PopularGamesStrip` itself and its other caller (`app/dashboard/nxlabs/page.tsx`) were left untouched.

**Concurrency note:** A sibling agent was actively committing directly to this same `/opt/nxeon` working tree during the session (confirmed via `git reflog` — commit `9b5f322d82`, a hero-gradient fix touching the same per-family page file). This caused one transient file-thrash scare; I verified the final on-disk state via `git diff`/checksum before proceeding, and there was no data loss. This repo also has a `post-commit` hook that auto-pushes to `origin main` in the background — my commit `2ec2214f7c` pushed itself immediately; I did not run `deploy-staging.sh` or `promote-production.sh` at any point.

**Files touched:** `/opt/nxeon/lib/mods-catalog.ts`, `/opt/nxeon/app/(marketing)/mods/page.tsx`, `/opt/nxeon/app/(marketing)/mods/games/[family]/page.tsx`, `/opt/nxeon/components/marketing/gamelanding/GameLandingCombined.tsx`, `/opt/nxeon/components/marketing/gamelanding/PlanConfigurator.tsx` (new), `/opt/nxeon/components/mods/GameCatalogueGrid.tsx` (new). `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. Real Playwright screenshots weren't taken — the two running `next-server` instances (ports 3000/3001) are serving the pre-existing build, not this uncommitted code, and getting a real screenshot of the new sections would have required a build, which was out of scope per the no-deploy directive.
